text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
TennisPlayer(x) ::: x is a tennis player.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are one of the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, i) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) ∧ FemalePlayer(x) → LostTo(x, Świątek)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) → (FemalePlayer(x) ∨ MalePlayer(x))) ::: All tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (MalePlayer(x) ∧ AtRolandGarros2022(x) → LostTo(x, Nadal)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
( (RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∨ LostTo(CocoGauff, Nadal)) → ¬MalePlayer(CocoGauff) ) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros2022(CocoGauff) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.
